affordance_in_statement: A group of three steps is classified as an unresolvable bottleneck if every single one of these 8 possible assignments results in at least one tool collision where both of the colliding steps belong to this group.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal: for three vertices, being non-2-colorable is mathematically equivalent to containing all three pairwise collision edges. Hiding the 2^3 explanation would only obscure, not remove, the shortcut.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the bottleneck as a triangle and enumerates triples in lexicographic order.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: There are exactly 2^3 = 8 assignments, and every assignment must contain an internal collision.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses constant-time adjacency checks to locate the lexicographically smallest triangle.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Every collision pair is an edge between two of the three selected steps.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Explicitly reduces the task to finding a triangle.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: "We need to find a triangle in the graph, which is an unresolvable bottleneck."

common_affordance: For exactly three vertices and two lines, every assignment has an internal same-line collision if and only if the three vertices form a triangle.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The visible code uses the same triangle reduction but performs nested triple enumeration with adjacency-set checks, giving impractical worst-case work near O(nm) or O(n^3) under the stated limits; the excerpt shows no different semantic interpretation.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat all survivors while preserving the task: the triangle reduction is the intrinsic mathematical structure of the required condition. Any edit that removes it must change the condition or the requested result.
